title: What’s Not on the Plate? Rethinking Food Computing through Indigenous Indian Datasets

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitatively evaluating existing food computing datasets and knowledge graphs to identify the underrepresentation of indigenous, traditional, and community-authored culinary practices compared to industrially structured, standardized, and Western-centric food data.
Analyzing existing food knowledge documentation to highlight the dominance of English-language data and the corresponding lack of representation for regional, vernacular, and endangered languages.

Examining current food datasets for their failure to capture local agroecologies, seasonal foraging patterns, and rural household practices, which are typically ignored in favor of globally commodified food data.
